title: SLO adaptive-threshold autotuner and anomaly scorer for paging prioritization
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our current SLO alerting relies on static thresholds and simple burn-rate windows which causes frequent noisy pages during short-lived spikes (eg. downstream GC storms, aggregator lag) and misses slow-degrading patterns that cross multiple signals. We also lack a unified way to attach trace context to metric anomalies, making root-cause handoff to oncall slower.

Goal: Build an adaptive SLO threshold autotuner plus an anomaly scoring service that synthesizes traces, metrics, and logs to produce a per-route anomaly score and a pagable priority. The system should: 1) reduce noisy pages (low-value alerts) by suppressing short-lived non-actionable spikes, 2) surface slowly degrading regressions earlier via drift-aware baselines, and 3) attach enriched trace snippets to prioritized pages for faster diagnosis.

Scope: design and implement the autotuner service, a scorer that combines EWMA baseline drift correction + seasonal decomposition + ensemble anomaly detector (statistical + isolation-forest fallback), trace-hook enrichment that captures the top-3 correlated spans and recent error logs, changes to metrics/log pipeline to emit event fragments to the scorer, and console dashboard widgets for score heatmap and paging policy simulation.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Autotuner computes route-level adaptive thresholds and publishes them to the AlertConfig service without human intervention for 80% of low-traffic routes.
2) Anomaly scorer generates a normalized score (0-100) and a priority label (info/warn/critical) that matches historical incident labels >= 85% F1 in backtest on last 12 months.
3) Paging noise reduced: >30% fewer P2/P1 pages during transient spikes in the 14-day canary window compared to current config.
4) Trace snippets and top-3 suspicious spans are present in page payloads for critical pages.
5) Rollout supports shadowing, canary at 10% routes, and full opt-in/out per-team via Console.
implementation_notes:
Architecture: new small Go service (slo-autotune) consumes downsampled metrics (1s/10s) and event fragments from the braided metrics/log pipeline (Kafka topic observ-event-fragments). It stores short-term state in Redis for EWMA and a longer-term model snapshot in S3. The anomaly scorer runs lightweight ML ensemble (stats + isolation-forest) in Rust via a shared library for low latency. Trace-hook change: tracing SDK will add a 64-byte indexable span signature and sample id to the event fragment to allow fast fetch of full spans by the scorer when score > threshold.

Dataflow changes: update the metrics router to fanout 1% of raw traces + event fragments to the new topic for training; fanout will be configurable per-tenant. Add a transform in the logs pipeline to extract error stack signatures and attach to fragments.

Operational: aim for <50ms added end-to-end scoring latency for decision path. Autoscaling: single replica per 10k RPS-equivalent of aggregated routes, with horizontal scaling policy tied to backlog depth.

Telemetry: new metrics: autotuner.baseline_drift_{route}, scorer.score_distribution, scorer.false_positive_estimate, paging.suppressed_count, paging.promoted_count.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (now-2w): instrumentation + synthetic backtests. Create synthetic workloads (latency spikes, slow drift, downstream error bursts) and run scorer offline to validate precision/recall.
Phase 1 (2-4w): Shadow mode on 10% low-risk routes, no paging changes; record score -> retrospective incident mapping.
Phase 2 (4-6w): Canary release to 10% routes for automatic suppression of low-value pages and enrichment on critical pages. Provide toggle per-team.
Phase 3 (6-10w): Gradual ramp to 100% with monitoring and rollback playbooks. Post-rollout 30-day burn metric review and tune.
test_plan: Unit tests for EWMA baseline and drift detector. Integration tests with simulated Kafka event fragments and a test Redis/S3. Backtest suite: 12-month historical replay with ground-truth incidents and noise injection. Load test: synthetic 50k routes to validate scaling and latency. QA checklist includes verification of: correct trace snippet attachment, per-route opt-out, dashboard score visualization, and paging policy simulator matching actual pages during canary.
risks_mitigation:
Risk: Over-suppression may hide real incidents. Mitigation: default conservative thresholds, shadowing for 2 weeks, and 'safety net' hard alert for aggregate SLO burn over longer window (24h) that bypasses suppression.
Risk: Privacy/regulatory concerns with trace fragments. Mitigation: scrub sensitive fields in transform, enforce tenant-level fanout opt-in, and KMS encryption for stored snippets.
Risk: Model drift / concept shift. Mitigation: daily backtests, automatic rollback if false_positive_estimate exceeds 20%.
